GainsBlock.rationale: `public override bool GainsBlock => true` (TrueGrit.cs:16) == the class attribute.

ctor.rationale: `base(1, CardType.Skill, CardRarity.Common, TargetType.Self)` (TrueGrit.cs:22-25) == cost 1 / SKILL / COMMON / SELF. True Grit has no Exhaust keyword of its own -- the Exhaust hover tip (TrueGrit.cs:20) refers to the card it exhausts -- and the sim leaves `exhausts` False.

CanonicalVars.rationale: `new BlockVar(7m, ValueProp.Move)` (TrueGrit.cs:18) == `_block = 7`. Move without Unpowered -> POWERED block, so NOT in gap G1's blast radius.

OnPlay.rationale: Both branches and the RNG are right. Block first on both sides (TrueGrit.cs:29). UPGRADED: `CardSelectCmd.FromHand(prefs: (ExhaustSelectionPrompt, 1), filter: null)` then exhaust the result if non-null (30-38) == `CardSelectCmd.from_hand(ctx.hooks, ctx.player, 'exhaust')` then exhaust `chosen[0]`. UN-UPGRADED: `Owner.RunState.Rng.CombatCardSelection.NextItem(pile.Cards)` over the WHOLE hand, not just Attacks (39-44) == the sim's parity branch `crng.card_selection.choice(ctx.player.hand)` with the shared legacy rng kept only for non-parity runs (true_grit.py:243-247). This is one of only five cards in the pool that route CombatCardSelection correctly (with cinder, infernal_blade, thrash and mad_science's Chaos rider). True Grit cannot exhaust itself on either side (Play pile in C#, discard-pile limbo in the sim). The sim's early `if not ctx.player.hand: return` covers C#'s two null checks at once. BLAST RADIUS on the upgraded branch, not re-verdicted per rule 3: `CardSelectCmd` auto-selects with no player choice and no RNG at or below MinSelect (CardSelectCmd.cs:287-290) -- creature_card_cmds steps 104/105.

OnUpgrade.rationale: `DynamicVars.Block.UpgradeValueBy(2m)` (TrueGrit.cs:49) == `self._block += 2` (7 -> 9). The upgrade ALSO swaps random selection for player choice, which lives in OnPlay's `IsUpgraded` branch rather than in a var -- the sim reads `self.upgrade_level > 0` at the same point.
